I had an earlier and larger Panda XPB45.... that lasted about 3 years and and over a thousand washes and was satisfied with it. This of course is a smaller unit. Outside of a simple gravity feed unlike the larger unit both the washer and spinner are strong. The so-called soft setting is the only one I use as its back and forth agitation is more efficient than the "stronger" one-way setting. I have put delicates & bras in the agitator and it has not ripped them apart. If there are sharp ends on bras or other items that might damage other garments I would put them in a small garment bag. I would not put my stiff jeans in this type of machine as I would be concerned with machine longevity but soft leggings are fine. This handles pillow cases, tops, shirts, undergarments, socks, bed sheets & hats but I would also beg off sneakers, comforters and heavy duty pullovers due to stress on the machine. I only wash clothes in cold water. From my own experience, even using hot water from the faucet will loosen seals and cause leaks. As far as lint goes, I've had it from the best machines. The floating lint traps don't work and it's more effective to use an electric lint shaver you can get from Amazon. It takes a little more time but it's more effective. Kind of a joke to call this 4 "layers" but it seems a bit better than just foil.... TLDR: It's a marginal step up from the complete trash foil only ones.

If you peel this stuff apart you will easily discover 2 layers. One being the thin PVC outer coating and the other being foil. I'm guessing the supposed first 3 layers, if they in fact exist, are a ridiculously thin layer of foil, then "PET", which I'm assuming is essentially just adhesive or something so thin it might as well be, then another ridiculously thin layer of foil followed by the PVC. The foil-PET-foil layers seem to be the same thickness as a run of the mill foil only duct. And the PVC layer is nothing particularly substantial either. So what you end up with is a standard thickness foil duct with a thin PVC outer coating. It appears much less substantial than anything someone with integrity would tout as "4 layers". There may technically be 4 layers of something there but 3 of them are so thin it might as well be a standard foil duct with a PVC layer. Unless standard foil ducts are 3 layers to begin with.

Anyway, all that being said, it's pretty much what I expected because I've learned to expect the cheapest, chintzyest crap possible to still marginally be whatever it claims to be. And it does honestly seem like a little step up from the absolute trash standard foil duct durability-wise with the PVC shell on it. And yes I know they're meant to be replaced every few years but who does that benefit? Not me or my finances. Not the environment. Keep getting nickle and dimed buying more disposable junk rather than being able to buy something that can survive a cleaning or even being handled or moved more than twice. Great plan. So yeah, I would choose this stuff over the foil only stuff. But the manufacturing world can and should do better
